tob-10501: This volume sets three English translations of the Qur’an — by Abdullah Yusuf Ali, Marmaduke Pickthall, and Mohammad Habib Shakir — in parallel columns for easy comparison. Readers can see how each translator handles the same Arabic verse, from the opening surah to the last. It is an ideal tool for anyone studying Islam’s scripture in English.
tob-10801: The poet and critic Matthew Arnold delivered these lectures to awaken English readers to the beauty of Welsh and Irish poetry. He praised the Celts’ delicate imagination and contrasted it with what he saw as Saxon stolidity. The lectures helped spark the Celtic revival in literature, influencing writers from Yeats onward.
tob-0101: Mathers’s Lemegeton — the Lesser Key — rolls the seventy-two Goetic demons with their seals and charges, besides works on angels and hours. It is the spell-book behind numberless latter-day wonder-workers. The edition stays the standard English text.
tob-9101: Griffith’s Atharva Veda turns the fourth Veda — hymns of spell, healing, and daily life in olden India. His verse-Englishing made these earthy charms sing in our tongue. Here are village and field, not the high gods’ court. The work opened the Veda’s folk side to western readers.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FerrieDavidWill: This item — Ferrie, David William: Civil Air Patrol 301 File — is a National Security Internet Archive file. The file’s full context is unclear. Ferrie was a Garrison-probe figure. The file may hold a clue. The item is a fragment of the archive.
voyages-of-samuel-de-champlain-volume-01: Samuel de Champlain, the founder of Quebec, recorded his explorations of northeastern North America in these famous journals. This first volume covers his early voyages along the Atlantic coast and into the interior he would claim for France. A foundational document of Canadian history, written by the man who lived it.
sidonia-the-sorceress-the-supposed-destr: This edition of Meinhold's haunting novel brings the story of Sidonia von Bork — the Pomeranian noblewoman tried as a witch — to English readers. Dark pacts, doomed dukes, and sixteenth-century superstition fill its pages. A landmark of gothic literature, as chilling now as when it first appeared.
the-adventures-of-ferdinand-count-fathom: Tobias Smollett's dark comic novel follows Ferdinand Count Fathom — gambler, swindler, and one of fiction's great villains — through his early career of roguery. This first volume launches his adventures across Europe. Smollett's savage humor and vivid lowlife scenes make it a landmark of the eighteenth-century novel.
the-thirty-years-war-volume-01: Friedrich Schiller — better known as Germany's great dramatist — was also a historian of power, and this opening volume begins his account of Europe's devastating Thirty Years War. The Bohemian revolt and the war's early campaigns unfold with a playwright's sense of drama. History written by a poet.
history-of-the-revolt-of-the-netherlands: Schiller opens his history of the Dutch revolt against Spain — the eighty-year struggle that created the Netherlands. This first volume sets the scene: Spanish oppression, the rise of William of Orange, and a people's awakening. Written with the passion of a lover of liberty.
abraham-lincoln-a-history-volume-01: John Nicolay and John Hay — Lincoln's own secretaries — wrote this monumental ten-volume life from unparalleled inside knowledge. This first volume covers Lincoln's origins and rise. The definitive nineteenth-century biography, it remains an essential source for understanding the man and his times.
the-prince-of-india-or-why-constantinopl: Lew Wallace — author of Ben-Hur — opens his epic of the fall of Constantinople in 1453. The mysterious Prince of India, a Wandering Jew figure, moves through the doomed city's last days. This first volume sets the stage for one of the great historical novels of the nineteenth century.
the-antiquary-volume-01: Walter Scott's Antiquary opens with Jonathan Oldbuck — the lovable, blustering student of ruins — and the coastal mysteries of northeast Scotland. This first volume sets one of Scott's most warmly human novels in motion, introducing the beggar Edie Ochiltree and a tangle of secrets. Antiquarian charm and romantic intrigue.
rob-roy-volume-01: Walter Scott opens his beloved Highland tale with young Frank Osbaldistone, cast off by his father and bound for the North. There he meets the gallant outlaw Rob Roy and the high-spirited Diana Vernon. This first volume sets one of literature's great adventures in motion.
arxiv-2605-08801: Forecasting traffic from data is easy to overdo: a model can memorize yesterday's jams instead of learning patterns that hold tomorrow. Peter Vanya, Katarína Šimková, and Rastislav Farkaš build data-driven transport models with built-in guards against overfitting, so the predictions stay honest on unseen days. The 2026 paper is applied modeling meant for real transit planning.
arxiv-2605-08901: The FitzHugh-Nagumo equations are the classic toy model of a firing neuron, and coupling many of them weakly and nonlocally produces traveling waves. N.I. Semenova, V.V. Semenov, and A.V. Bukh push such systems with extreme forcing and study the resulting wave dynamics. The 2026 paper is nonlinear dynamics on excitable media.
arxiv-2605-09201: STT-MRAM stores bits in the magnetization of tiny magnets, flipped by spin-polarized currents. Afan Terko, George Lertzman-Lepofsky, Dieter Suess, and colleagues study magnetization alignment in these memories. The 2026 paper is device physics for the next generation of RAM.
arxiv-2605-09301: Delivery trucks with limited capacity need routes planned in one shot, not endless re-optimization. Samuel J. K. Chin and Maximilian Schiffer cluster first with neural networks, then route second, via differentiable optimization. The 2026 paper is vehicle routing learned end to end.
arxiv-2605-09401: Chimera states — networks where order and chaos coexist — are as beautiful as they are baffling. Rommel Tchinda Djeudjo, Riccardo Muolo, Thierry Njougouo, and colleagues classify them with Fourier analysis and unsupervised learning. The 2026 paper taxonomizes the half-ordered world of coupled oscillators.
arxiv-2605-09501: Active nematics — swirling fluids of self-driven rods, like bacterial soups — go unstable in beautiful patterns. I.K. Joseph, A.J.H. Houston, K.N. Kowal, and N.J. Mottram study how an orienting field steers that instability and selects the modes. The 2026 paper is soft-matter physics on living liquid crystals.
arxiv-2605-09701: Self-driving cars must imagine what happens next — pedestrians stepping out, cars swerving, sudden stops. Yufeng Hong, Xiaotian Zhou, Yingyan Li, and colleagues build DriveFuture: future-aware latent world models for autonomous driving. The 2026 paper gives robot drivers an imagination.
arxiv-2605-10001: Hypergraphs capture higher-order relations beyond pairwise edges; condensing them with anchor guidance and dual-level discrimination preserves structure. Fan Li, Xiaoyang Wang, Chen Chen, and Wenjie Zhang develop the method. The 2026 paper is graph learning that compresses without losing the plot.
arxiv-2605-10201: Robot manipulation that generalizes across heterogeneous object interactions — HeteroGenManip. Zhenhao Shen, Zeming Yang, Yue Chen, and colleagues build the generalizable system. The 2026 paper is robotics for diverse objects. It handles real object heterogeneity with true robotic grace. Diverse objects, one graceful policy.
pmc-13521901: Gallium nitride thin films — anisotropic thermal transport mapped in space and time with ultrafast X-ray diffraction. Thanh Nguyen, Chuliang Fu, Mouyang Cheng, and colleagues do the mapping. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is thermal materials science. It watches heat flow unevenly through GaN.
pmc-13418201: Risk stratification in cardiovascular medicine — from atrial fibrillation to the broader disease spectrum, for prognosis and therapeutic decisions. Yuichi Saito, Kazuya Tateishi, Ken Kato, and colleagues review the tools. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is cardiology. It stratifies cardiac risk across diseases.
pmc-13421601: Buddhist Highest Yoga Tantra meditation — reproducible neural states evidenced by EEG. E V Mikhaylets, A М Razorenova, V L Chernyshev, and colleagues record the meditators. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is meditation neuroscience. It finds the same brain states in deep tantra.
pmc-13422801: Adolescent and young adult status inconsistently reported in non-interventional cancer research — a critical barrier to evidence usability. Katja Reuter, David R Freyer, Joel Milam, and colleagues document the inconsistency. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is research methodology. It shows sloppy AYA reporting wasting evidence.
pmc-13518101: A ruptured cerebral arteriovenous malformation — initially managed as presumed eclampsia, a diagnostic challenge in a resource-limited setting. Mirza Muflihul Haque, Debashish Banik, Mahbub Nisat Ibtasam, and colleagues report the case. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is a diagnostic case. It unmasks a brain bleed mimicking eclampsia.
pmc-13455001: Acidic microenvironments — how pH sensing links them to immune reprogramming in inflammation. Mingyu Zhang, Jiaju Tian, and Weiming Sun review the mechanisms. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is immuno-metabolism. It shows acid rewriting immune behavior. Acidic niches, immunologically active. pH sensing, reviewed.
arxiv-2606-17201: Violeta Mar and Gustavo Boska describe ends and tangles, ways of capturing a graph's infinite structure, through Boolean algebras and functors. Ends are the directions to infinity; tangles are the highly connected regions. The categorical reformulation unifies these tools, giving graph theorists a cleaner language for the infinite.
arxiv-2606-18101: Jingyuan Huang and colleagues distill GUI grounding with quality-aware self-distillation, trusting the right teacher. The student model learns where to click from the most reliable of its own predictions. Quality awareness prevents learning from mistakes. The method sharpens AI agents that operate software.
arxiv-2606-18201: Zhengfeng Ji, Yinchen Liu, and Zhe'ou Zhou tackle the complexity of the circuit width problem. Circuit width measures parallelizability, and its complexity was open. Their results place the problem in the complexity zoo. The paper is theoretical computer science at its sharpest.
arxiv-2606-18401: H. Terças and V. N. Mantsevich find negative diffusivity of excitons in electron-hole plasmas. Instead of spreading, the bound electron-hole pairs clump together. The counterintuitive result reshapes models of semiconductor plasmas. It matters for lasers and optoelectronics built on these materials.
plos-pone-0003401: Marine ecologists found a coral traveling farther than expected in this 2008 genetics study. The species mostly recruits its own offspring locally, yet DNA traces revealed recent long-distance dispersal between separated populations. Mapping that hidden connectivity matters for reef conservation, since protected areas only work if young corals actually move between them.
plos-pone-0003501: Public-health researchers found faster tests are not enough in this 2008 South African study. Offering rapid same-day HIV test results to a rural community did not reliably raise testing uptake, showing that speed alone does not overcome the barriers people face. The results argue that counseling, stigma, and access need attention alongside the technology.
plos-pone-0003601: HIV researchers Saïdi, Melki, and Gougeon caught killer cells waking a sleeping virus in this 2008 paper. When natural killer cells attack dendritic cells, the released HMGB1 signal triggered HIV-1 replication and persistence in the survivors. The finding reveals how immune crosstalk can inadvertently switch the virus back on.
plos-pone-0003701: In 2008, Sun, Chen, and Hou built universal PCR primers from locked nucleic acids. Their five-letter LNA pentamers can kick off DNA copying across the genome, a tool for amplifying many targets at once. The design saves time, cost, and labor in labs that need to read lots of DNA fast.
plos-pone-0003801: Hacker, Lee, and Rathmell found some VHL mutations keeping their day job in this 2008 paper. Type 2B mutations of the von Hippel-Lindau gene retained the VBC complex's form and function. The retained function helps explain why these mutations produce their particular tumor spectrum.
plos-pone-0003901: A 2008 pediatric study auditioned a better TB blood marker for kids. Whittaker, Gordon, and Kampmann compared IP-10 against interferon-gamma for telling active from latent tuberculosis in children. The head-to-head test seeks a clearer signal for young patients.
plos-pone-0004001: In 2008, Lopez, Textoris, and Bergon built a browser for gene-activity data. TranscriptomeBrowser mines the growing public microarray repositories with a flexible toolbox. The tool helps researchers productively explore the vast transcriptional landscape of cells. The software turns public data overload into navigable biological insight for all.
plos-pone-0004101: In 2008, a US team found Lyme germs loosening mouse blood vessels. Broth from virulent Borrelia burgdorferi made the vessels leak more. Single mouse vessels, perfused alone, leaked badly after exposure. The leakiness may explain how Lyme spreads through body tissues.
plos-pone-0004201: In 2009, Ling, Song, and Garza watched Alzheimer's poison work in flies. Abeta42 triggered age-dependent neurodegeneration through autophagic-lysosomal injury. The peptide wrecked the cell's recycling system. The fly model exposes a druggable choke point. The mechanism may explain late-onset brain cell loss.
plos-pone-0004301: In 2009, Watanabe, Suzuki, and Ishikawa found wild mice with broken body clocks. Genetic analysis of wild-derived arrhythmic mice revealed a new circadian variant. The variant's rhythm faded after brief initial upkeep. The mice offer a fresh clock model for research.
plos-pone-0004401: In 2009, Karita, Ketter, and Price set healthy baselines for African labs. Hematology and biochemistry reference intervals for healthy adults in eastern and southern Africa were derived. The local ranges replace foreign standards in trials. The work sharpens clinical trials across Africa. The baselines fill a long-standing gap.
plos-pone-0004501: In 2009, a team found antimicrobial bits doubling as cell signals. Two chromogranin A-derived bits induced calcium entry in human neutrophils. The bits opened calcium gates via calmodulin control. The finding links nerves to white-cell immunity. The bits are fully natural bits.
plos-pone-0004601: In 2009, Bibby, Zhang, and Chen mapped the ocean's sunlight catchers. Biogeography of photosynthetic light-harvesting genes in marine phytoplankton was charted. The cyanobacterial genera dominated the samples fully. The study maps marine energy flow today. The tiny proteins harvest light efficiently.
plos-pone-0004701: In 2009, Albrecht-Buehler sketched a bold genome navigation system. An outline of a genome navigation system based on GA-sequences was proposed. The tetra-GA motifs guided the map well. The paper offers a visualization method anew. The motif chains are shared.
plos-pone-0358701: How do a country’s rules shape what policies its leaders prefer? This paper uses Bayesian structural equation modeling to trace the links between institutional frameworks and policy preferences. The analysis maps how governance structures steer decisions, giving reformers a clearer model of what actually drives policy choices.
plos-pone-0356801: Hearts don’t beat in isolation — coupling between heart-rate signals reveals hidden health. This paper evaluated heart rate coupling with multi-dimensional recurrence quantification analysis and cross-correlation, carefully weighing the analytical decisions. The methodological comparison guides researchers choosing how to measure the heart’s subtle rhythms.
plos-pone-0357601: Dandruff’s culprit, Malassezia furfur, forms stubborn biofilms that resist treatment. This study tested Angelica dahurica–Ligusticum sinense plant extracts for inhibitory effect and safety against the fungus and its biofilms. The extracts offer a natural alternative to harsh antifungal chemicals.
plos-pone-0357301: Red mud — the caustic waste of aluminum production — can be reborn as concrete, but sulfate in soil attacks it. This paper tested the sulfate resistance of polyvinyl alcohol and basalt fiber-reinforced red mud concrete. The results show whether this waste-based concrete can survive harsh ground conditions.
plos-pone-0357901: Railway disasters rarely have a single cause — they emerge from tangled risk networks. This paper identified critical risk factors in railway operations using directed weighted complex networks combined with combinatorial weighting-TOPSIS. The network analysis ranks which risks matter most, giving safety managers a prioritized hit list.
plos-pone-0356501: Reprogramming adult cells into stem cells appears to reset the epigenetic marks of aging. This paper characterized DNA methylation in PBMCs and donor-matched iPSCs, showing age-related methylation is reset during reprogramming. The reset offers a molecular glimpse of cellular rejuvenation in action.
plos-pone-0357501: The PreserFlo MicroShunt offers surgical drainage for glaucoma — but results vary by glaucoma type. This matched analysis compared outcomes in primary open-angle versus pseudoexfoliative glaucoma. The comparison gives surgeons evidence for choosing — or avoiding — the device in each case.
plos-pone-0355301: A new class of operators extends the classical theory of Hilbert spaces. This paper defined the polynomially quasi-mth-Helton class of Hilbert space operators and explored its mathematical properties. The abstract results enrich operator theory — the deep mathematics underlying quantum mechanics and signal processing.
plos-pone-0356201: Symmetries of spacetime reveal deep physics. This comparative study examined homothetic symmetries of static plane symmetric spacetimes across different energy-momentum tensor representations. The mathematical classification sharpens our picture of how matter shapes geometry.
plos-pone-0357101: After stroke clot removal, drug therapy still decides outcomes — and pharmacists can optimize it. This pre- and post-intervention study measured the impact of a pharmacist-led optimization strategy for cerebrovascular pharmacotherapy beyond recanalization in acute ischemic stroke. The pharmacists measurably improved care.
plos-pone-0338001: Too many kidney patients get referred to specialists tragically late. This analysis of referral patterns in Australia’s CKD.QLD Registry calls for revisiting the very definition of ‘late referral.’ The data-driven argument could reshape when — and how urgently — kidney care begins.
plos-pone-0353201: What do Muslim religious leaders around the world actually think about climate change? This international survey asked them directly. Their views — spanning theology, science, and policy — reveal both surprising consensus and deep divides. The findings matter because these leaders shape the beliefs and behaviors of nearly two billion people.
plos-pone-0356601: Adolescents who self-injure show altered brain function — and resting-state fMRI can see it. This study examined altered brain function associated with non-suicidal self-injury in adolescents with major depressive disorder. The neural signatures could one day guide interventions for these vulnerable teens.
plos-pone-0352701: Harvesting cherry tomatoes by robot needs a gentle, precise gripper. This paper optimized a bionic end-effector for automated harvesting using Response Surface Methodology and Box-Behnken design. The carefully tuned gripper picks ripe tomatoes without bruising — bringing robotic harvest closer to the greenhouse.
plos-pone-0356001: Formalin-free tissue preservation could transform pathology — if nucleic acids survive. This paper demonstrated good DNA and sufficient RNA integrity in formalin-free paraffin-embedded tissues. The findings validate an alternative that spares lab workers formalin’s toxicity while preserving molecular analyzability.
plos-pone-0355401: Pediatric heart assist devices — keeping children’s failing hearts going — demand rigorous safety oversight. This paper analyzed adverse event reporting and regulation for these devices. The regulatory analysis exposes where surveillance protects young patients — and where dangerous gaps remain.
plos-pone-0355601: Medical Internet of Things devices — from monitors to implants — need intrusion detection that preserves privacy. FedMamba-IoMT combines federated state space models with differential privacy and Byzantine resilience for exactly that. The privacy-preserving detector guards patients’ devices without exposing their data.
plos-pone-0355101: Children exposed to prescription opioids in the womb — how do they fare in kindergarten? This paper examined teacher-reported development among these children. The classroom-based findings reveal the developmental footprint of prenatal opioid exposure — informing early intervention.
plos-pone-0354801: Toddler’s fractures — tiny shin breaks — may not need casting at all. This multicentre non-inferiority RCT protocol will test no-immobilisation against traditional immobilisation. The planned trial could free thousands of toddlers — and their parents — from unnecessary casts.
plos-pone-0355201: Thailand’s pharmacogenomic landscape — how genes shape drug response — was unmapped at scale. This paper profiled it with array-based testing linked to electronic medical records of medication exposure. The findings bring precision prescribing closer for 70 million Thais.
plos-pone-0354701: Surgery is frightening — but does counseling or technique choice ease preoperative anxiety? This paper investigated both. The findings tell surgeons and anesthesiologists what actually calms patients before the scalpel — words, methods, or both.
plos-pone-0352901: Geotextile tubes — giant sand-filled flood barriers — fail by seepage scour when sidewalls damage. This experimental study examined that failure in tube gaps. The findings guide engineers toward barriers that hold when waters rise — and knowledge of exactly how they break.
plos-pone-0353801: Measuring elbow range of motion — clinically, without markers stuck to skin — would simplify assessment. This paper validated markerless human pose estimation methods for that clinical task. The validation compared AI-estimated angles against gold-standard measurements. The methods proved accurate enough for clinical use. The findings bring computer vision into the physiotherapy clinic — no markers, no hassle.
plos-pone-0354601: High-risk prostate cancer staging — whole-body MRI with diffusion weighting and background suppression. This paper assessed its efficacy and limitations. The imaging evaluation revealed what the technique catches and what it misses. The findings guide urologists on when this radiation-free staging justifies its cost and complexity.
plos-pone-0345901: Lung cancer caregivers — their health literacy — determines the care patients receive. This cross-sectional survey measured its current status. The findings revealed gaps in caregivers’ ability to navigate complex oncology. The research argues that supporting the supporter — through targeted health literacy — is itself a cancer intervention.
plos-pone-0354301: Strip-shaped deep white matter hyperintensities — possibly marking neurodegeneration. This diffusion tensor imaging study explored the link. The findings suggested these stripe patterns reflect dying neural connections. The research offers radiologists a new signpost — white matter’s stripes as degeneration’s signature.
plos-pone-0344401: Early DNA methylation at the NR3C1 promoter’s NGFI-A site — predicting cognition at age five. This Parents as Teachers intervention study provided the evidence. The epigenetic mark forecasted childhood cognitive function. The findings linked early experience, written in methyl groups, to the developing mind — biology’s memory of nurture.
plos-pone-0352201: Omicron COVID-19 — its primary infection’s skin manifestations. This paper documented them. The dermatological catalog distinguished Omicron’s cutaneous signatures. The findings aided diagnosis — the skin as the virus’s bulletin board.
plos-pone-0353301: Mosquito bed nets — their impact on malaria transmission and pyrethroid resistance evolution modeled. This paper did so. The findings revealed the double-edged sword — nets saving lives while selecting resistance. The research guided vector control — the evolutionary chess game, played wisely.
plos-pone-0353701: Emergency SAT1 foot-and-mouth disease vaccine — monovalent — comprehensively evaluated. This paper assessed antigen quality, product consistency, and protective efficacy. The findings validated a vaccine for outbreak emergencies. The research protected livestock — and the livelihoods depending on them.
plos-pone-0353401: Uzbek coronary patients — monogenic familial hypercholesterolemia detected by next-generation sequencing. This paper measured the genetic yield. The findings revealed hidden inherited cholesterol disorders. The research brought the precision — to Central Asian cardiology. The Uzbek focus fills a gap: Central Asian populations are nearly absent from familial hypercholesterolemia genetics literature.
plos-pone-0318901: Japanese amebiasis — epidemiological characteristics from 2001 to 2022. This paper did so. The findings tracked two decades of the parasite. The research mapped the infection — the amoeba’s Japanese history. The 2001-2022 span captures the trend: two decades showing whether the parasite is advancing or retreating.
plos-pone-0349701: Sesame plants — ginger-loaded chitosan nanoparticles affecting growth, morphology, and biochemistry. This paper tested the effects. The findings explored nano-delivered ginger as a crop stimulant. Its novelty lies in the delivery vehicle. The work brings nanomedicine’s tricks to the sesame field.
plos-pone-0351701: Pancreatic cancer cell subpopulations — mitochondrial metabolic pathway mechanisms from single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing. This paper uncovered them. The analysis mapped how distinct tumor cells power themselves. Its therapeutic hint is metabolic targeting. The work exposes the cancer’s energy secrets, cell by cell.
plos-pone-0350401: Shelter dogs — stress, metabolism, and fecal microbiota linked to shelter conditions in a multisystem analysis. This paper did so. The analysis connected housing to the dog’s whole biology. Its welfare message is housing matters. The work reads the kennel’s toll in the dog’s gut.
plos-pone-0352401: One Health research organization — gendered male and high-income country authors dominating publication. This paper documented it. The analysis counted the bylines’ bias. Its equity value is the exposure. The work names the publishing’s skewed voice. The One Health setting is the irony: a field preaching interconnectedness publishes through a narrow demographic.
plos-pone-0342601: Quantity surveyors — their evolving roles in achieving the UN sustainable development goals. This paper examined them. The analysis reimagined the cost consultant as a sustainability agent. The finding expands the profession’s mandate. The work recasts the bean-counter as a planet-saver.
plos-pone-0352501: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia — extracellular vesicle microRNAs as a biomarker discovery platform. This paper explored the potential. The vesicles’ tiny RNAs may flag the childhood leukemia. The finding opens a liquid-biopsy avenue. The work seeks the cancer’s signature in circulating bubbles.
plos-pone-0350801: Probiotics and dietary intake — pilot data from a randomized sub-study of the ProBioHRV trial in depressed patients and healthy controls. This paper asked whether probiotics modulate eating. The analysis tested the gut’s vote on the menu. The finding is preliminary. The work wonders whether the microbes choose our meals.
plos-pone-0335301: Flour beetle inbreeding avoidance — pre- and post-copulatory, tested in Tribolium castaneum. This paper did so. The analysis watched the beetles choose mates. The finding is the avoidance. The work asks whether the flour beetle shuns its kin. The pre/post-copulatory split is the thoroughness: it tests avoidance both in mate choice and in sperm use after mating.
plos-pone-0352101: Travel consultation success — a particular state’s occurrence predicting it. This paper demonstrated the predictor. The analysis found the mindset that forecasts the good consult. The finding is the state. The work predicts the traveler’s successful visit. The ‘particular state’ is the psychology: the paper identifies the traveler’s mindset that predicts a fruitful consultation.
europmc-pmc2855701: Immune-system simulations need good binding math, and this 2010 paper joins two crafts. The authors show how binding-prediction tools feed immune simulations in bioinformatics. Their blend made virtual immune runs more true to life. The piece bridged two coding camps and pointed to a future where computers pre-test vaccine ideas.
europmc-pmc2883601: Simulating molecules needs water models that behave right. This 2010 paper builds a polarizable water model for the coarse-grained MARTINI force field used in molecular dynamics. The authors' upgrade adds realism without heavy cost. Their model improved a widely used simulation toolkit for soft matter.
europmc-pmc3003701: Stressed cells mail guard messages in tiny bubbles. This 2010 paper shows cells release bubble-packets carrying guard signals during oxidant stress. The authors catch the mail in the act. Their work helped launch bubble-packet research. Neighboring cells heed the mailed warnings.
europmc-pmc3087801: Crop genotyping got cheap and simple. This 2011 paper brings a sturdy low-cost DNA-typing method for diverse crops. The authors' approach spread through breeding programs. Their work powered crop science. Breeders type thousands of plants per day. The method needs no prior genome.
europmc-pmc3097201: Serious mental illness shortens lives. This 2011 London study finds people with severe mental illness die years earlier. The authors' register data demands action. Their work shaped health equity. Heart disease, not suicide, led the toll. Clinics now screen minds and bodies together.
europmc-pmc3101201: Migration and health got a policy framework. This 2011 paper builds a framework for migrant health policy in our century. The authors guide policymakers. Their work shaped global health. The framework centers migrants' own voices. WHO adopted its core principles. The paper remains the field's benchmark.
europmc-pmc2929501: A DNA-damage beacon got reviewed. This 2010 paper surveys H2AX phosphorylation's role in the DNA damage response and cancer therapy. The authors map the signaling cascade. Their overview guides oncologists. Phosphorylated H2AX flags broken strands. Radiation oncologists track it to gauge dose.
europmc-pmc3146901: Malaria mosquitoes moved outdoors after spraying. This 2011 Bioko Island study tracks Anopheles mosquitoes' outdoor biting after vector control. The authors reveal the shift. Their work guides control strategy. Indoor spraying missed the outdoor biters. New traps target the evening crowd.
europmc-pmc3215701: Lab data analysis got user-friendly. This 2011 paper introduces Chipster, friendly software for microarray and high-throughput data. The authors' tool serves biologists. Their software spread through labs. Point-and-click replaced command lines. Teaching labs adopted it fast. The software is open source.
europmc-pmc3316601: Ancient DNA damage got timed. This 2012 paper maps how damage accumulates in ancient DNA. The authors reveal the clock. Their work guides paleogenetics. Pääbo's lab led the work. The clock dates old bones. The paper is widely cited. It shaped Neanderthal research.
europmc-pmc3348501: Brain-scan noise got a source. This 2012 paper traces body-signal noise in brain light scans. The authors reveal the origin. Their work guides brain imaging. Heartbeat leaked into the signal. Kirilina's team led the work. The paper is widely cited.
europmc-pmc3360701: Arthritis got an early warning. This 2012 paper shows spreading immune antibodies predict rheumatoid arthritis. The authors reveal the prediction. Their work guides prevention. Warnings came years before symptoms. Sokolove's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. It shaped screening.
europmc-pmc3395601: Pufferfish sex got a gene switch. This 2012 paper links an Amhr2 gene variant to sex in tiger pufferfish. The authors reveal the variant. Their work lights up biology. Kamiya's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. It is a classic.
europmc-pmc6520701: Obesity and high blood fats are leading risk factors for chronic kidney disease, and fat clogging kidney tissue appears to be why. This review traces how free fatty acids infiltrate the kidney, spark inflammation, and scar the filters. It connects lipid metabolism to kidney failure and points to fat-targeting strategies that might protect the kidneys.
europmc-pmc6524401: Interleukin 6 is an immune messenger that surges during viral infections, rallying defenses but sometimes fueling dangerous inflammation. This review examines IL-6's double-edged role across viral diseases: when it helps clear the virus and when its excess harms the host. The balance it strikes makes IL-6 both a marker of severe infection and a target for calming immune overreactions.
europmc-pmc6585101: Cancer immunotherapy matured fast: checkpoint blockers and engineered CAR-T cells moved from experiments to standard care. This 2019 roundup surveys the latest trends - new targets, smarter combinations, and efforts to help more patients respond. The field's momentum suggests immunotherapy will keep rewriting cancer treatment.
europmc-pmc6586801: When oxygen runs low, cells flip a master switch - the HIF pathway - that rewires metabolism, grows new vessels, and adapts tissues to thin air. This review traces hypoxia signaling across human disease, from cancer to heart failure, and the drugs aiming at it. Tuning this ancient oxygen sensor is a hot therapeutic frontier.
europmc-pmc6610901: Breaking a hip after 60 is dangerous - and many patients never fully recover. This study tracked death rates after osteoporotic hip fracture: how common, how trends shifted, and which factors raise the risk. The numbers guide prevention and tell families and doctors what to expect.
europmc-pmc6626501: Vitamin D does more than build bone - its receptor sits in tissues throughout the body. This review surveys the vitamin's skeletal and extraskeletal actions: immunity, cell growth, and more, plus the open questions. A century after rickets' cause was found, vitamin D still guards mysteries.
europmc-pmc6729001: Colorectal cancer spreads with help from an RNA-tagging enzyme: METTL3. This study shows the upregulated methyltransferase drives metastasis via the miR-1246/SPRED2/MAPK chain - adding methyl marks that unleash aggressive behavior.
